purpose: Assign probability mass to each possible return count and watch a complete distribution change while its total stays one.
meaning: A finite discrete probability distribution lists the possible values of a random variable and their probability masses. Nonnegative masses add to one. The support consists of the values with positive mass.

definition.setting: An assumed library return-desk model for X, the number of books at one future check-in: X has listed values 0,1,2.

signature.X: Random number of books at the next check-in.
signature.xᵢ: One of the three outcome values 0, 1 or 2 books.
signature.pᵢ: Probability P(X=xᵢ) assigned to outcome xᵢ.
signature.r: Share of the probability left after one-book outcomes, assigned to two books.

conditions: The random variable X counts books received at the next library check-in and takes values 0, 1 or 2. These probabilities form an assumed teaching model, not collected library data.
The controls q and r lie between 0 and 1 inclusive. q is the probability of one book; r assigns a share of the remaining probability to two books. The rest goes to zero books.
The probability mass function is p₀=(1−q)(1−r), p₁=q and p₂=(1−q)r. Each mass is nonnegative and their sum is one. A zero mass removes that outcome from the support.
A probability mass is dimensionless. Bar positions are whole book counts and bar heights are masses; no probability is assigned to points between the listed outcomes.
definition.domain_notes: This is a probability mass function on three listed values, not a probability density. The live primary result is P(X=2), one part of the full distribution.
definition.proof_status: Definition-level sources and original finite calculations; independent review pending.

grammar.formation_rule: Use q for the one-book probability. The remaining probability is 1−q; r sends its selected share to two books and 1−r sends the rest to zero books. Thus p₀=(1−q)(1−r), p₁=q and p₂=(1−q)r.
grammar.precedence: Form the remainder 1−q first, then split it using r and 1−r. Keep an outcome value separate from its probability.

prompts.prompt: Does zero probability remove a value from the displayed outcome list?
prompts.answer: The list can retain the label as a reference, but only positive-probability values belong to the support.

prompts.prompt: Why do the masses always add to one?
prompts.answer: The outer masses add to (1−q)((1−r)+r)=1−q, and the middle mass is q.
